rationale: Both candidates surface the same underlying ground-truth concern (trust_remote_code compatibility, found already fixed by a later commit, downgraded to a stale-PR-description nit), so recall is equal. X pads its report with roughly ten near-duplicate restatements of that single point (several with placeholder '?:line' paths), which dilutes precision and actionability even though its two genuinely novel findings (cache-before-validation bug, missing cache test) are solid. Y delivers a clean, non-redundant review with several deep, well-grounded, distinct findings (broad except swallowing transient errors, dead None-fallback on kernels≥0.15, missing cache-reset hook, uncovered test path) each with precise file/line and concrete fixes, making it far more useful despite comparable coverage of the sole ground-truth item.
